name: waulking songs

attributes.attribute: a work of shrinking wool until it was waterproof

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Waulking songs are a folkloric motif. Groups of women sang the songs as they waulked the wool. Waulking is the act of shrinking woven cloth to make it waterproof. The songs carried myth and folk references through oral handling. Oral tradition changes at a slow rate, so much of the song body stayed old. The rise of mechanical looms and wool machines cut the old singing custom into decline. Some groups did not let the songs pass. Scotland's Capercaillie put a set of these rhythmic songs onto record for a later audience.

okr.objective: Waulking songs are an old singing custom tied to the making of woolen cloth.
